proof.text: For the section-ring equality, apply sheaf and functor extensionality. At each object, additive structures coincide definitionally. Equality of products follows by evaluating the tensor compatibility of sheafToPresheaf with continuous pushforward on a pure tensor, then applying the coefficient multiplication. Ring extensionality supplies the bundled ring equality; naturality is the equality-transport equation for the same restriction maps. This is sectionRing_over_eq and its slice specialization in Lean.

The transported section equivalence is additive because every equivalence between these preadditive categories preserves binary products and zero morphisms. Apply Mathlib Functor.additive_of_preserves_binary_products directly; no elimination of the concrete section-ring equality is needed.

Project lem-pe-internal-section-tensor-comparison to the existential ordinary comparison together with its pure-tensor formula and its sum-total summand formula. This is sectionTensorWitness. The pure-tensor formula determines the ordinary maps by the relative tensor universal property, so sectionOrdinaryTensorIso is a choice of the canonical normalized data, not an arbitrary isomorphism. Specialize the retained sum-total formula to the slice ring and unfold only the ordinary-comparison alias to prove sliceRawComplexTensorComparison. Keeping the unused coherence, acyclicity and flatness clauses out of this choice predicate avoids repeated kernel comparison of their large dependent endpoint types.

Let the section-ring presentation vary over S with an equality from the reconstructed ring to S. Transport the section equivalence along that equality and form the type of isomorphisms between its image of the native cochain total and the coefficient total of its images. At reflexivity the fixed raw comparison inhabits this type, since both totals are their explicit sum totals. Equality elimination identifies every fiber with this reflexive fiber. The private complexAt_eq and totalTypeAt_eq rewrite its specialization to the existing sliceComplexForward endpoints without unfolding the tensors. Transport the raw isomorphism along the resulting type equality. HEq with that fixed isomorphism determines it uniquely by eq_of_heq, proving sliceTotalComparison_existsUnique.

Over an abstract closed braided Grothendieck abelian category, the framework native derived monoidal constructor is definitionally DerivedMonoidal.instMonoidalCategory for its K-flat localization. Prove this equality by reflexivity before specializing to the slice module category. The native tensor, internal Hom, braiding and evaluation remain the framework constructions, independently of any ringed-site closed structure. The same abstract argument is repeated privately for the existing global monoidal equality of the sole consumer, avoiding the same concrete unfolding there. Local named proofs of graded tensor coproduct existence and its associativity compatibility keep the native slice tensor proof arguments shared; their mathematical structures are unchanged.

title: Local internal module-object derived Hom and restriction comparison
statement: Let X be a scheme, J its small pro-etale site, Λ a commutative condensed ring, B=p_X^*Λ its coefficient ring object and A its category of internal module objects, with the global section-action derived equivalence and normalized tensor comparison of [def-sfb-internal-section-derived-tensor-comparison]. For every U in the site, let B_U=B|_U be the literal restricted commutative ring object [def-pur-localized-ringed-site], and A_U its actual module-object category [sk-def-sfb-module-objects]. Its reconstructed section ring equals B_sec|_U; the section-action equivalence [def-weil-pbc-internal-abelian-sheaf-module-equivalence] is additive, giving E_U=D(F_U) on the ordinary unbounded derived categories [sk-def-sfb-derived-categories]. Define internal restriction as E_U^{-1} r D(F), with its section comparison the equivalence counit. Use the framework's NATIVE K-flat derived relative tensor on D(A_U), its NATIVE MonoidalClosed.internalHom and the native adjunction counit [sk-def-sfb-derived-tensor-hom]; none is transported from a chosen ringed-site closed structure. The native monoidal instance equals its K-flat localization instance, which supplies the actual Koszul braiding; write its evaluation with Hom as first tensor factor using this braiding. For local internal complexes P,Q, the canonical sum-total comparison with the sectionwise total is uniquely characterized on EVERY summand p+q=n by the ordinary section-action pure-tensor comparison, with the reconstructed and restricted section-ring presentations identified by their equality. For a local K-injective Hom H_U [def-pur-derived-internal-hom], closed ringed data S_U and K-flat models T_U [def-coef-ringed-tensor-hom-model], define a SliceTensorComparison to be a natural isomorphism from E_U of the NATIVE local derived tensor to S_U.tensor(E_U(-),E_U(-)), whose localization square on EVERY pair of complexes with K-flat section images is the canonical sum-total comparison followed by T_U's K-flat comparison. Given such a t_U, normalized ringed restriction data d [def-sfb-ringed-slice-comparison-model] and a global Hom comparison θ, a SliceHomComparison consists of θ^U:E_U RHom^{A_U}_{B_U}≅H_U(E_U(-),E_U(-)), natural in ALL local derived objects, and its evaluation equation using the NATIVE local counit and t_U. It also contains a natural module-side restriction isomorphism r_U:r_int RHom^A_B≅RHom^{A_U}_{B_U}(r_int(-),r_int(-)). Its compatibility square says E_U(r_U), then θ^U and the Hom map of the restriction-section counits, equals the restriction-section counit at RHom^A_B, then r(θ), then d.eta. Thus r_U is the unique fully faithful lift of the square, whereas θ^U and t_U compare the independently given NATIVE structures. The same evaluation and restriction equations are also named as generic predicates on their category and functor endpoints; specializing these predicates to the canonical functors and native evaluations gives exactly the displayed conditions.
